pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql has a CHECK constraint and a default of 'normal'. test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that the existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
The 'AC-2' test checks the exact labels on high and low items and no label on normal ones.
The 'AC-3' test checks each filter and id order.
The 'AC-4' test checks that `/` lists every item in id order.
The 'AC-5' test checks the exact nav markup for all four views.
The 'AC-6' test checks a 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, an empty value and __proto__. The code checks a Set.
The 'AC-7' test checks the exact messages for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' in all four views of an empty table. The weakened state test does not change this, because AC-7 covers it.
traffic/routes.json contains /?priority=high, and the 'AC-8' test asserts it.

findings.what: The follow-up commit 'Follow-up edits' loosened the 'No match' state test from toBe("No low-priority items.") to toBeDefined(). `message()` returns null when there is no message, and null is defined, so the assertion can never fail. The state row 'No match' now has no exact check in the states block. The AC-7 test still covers the exact text, but the spec has no decision that justifies loosening a test.
The body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none'. This is false: the final commit loosened the 'No match' assertion to toBeDefined().
findings.fix: Restore the assertion and keep the claim, or state the loosening and why.

findings.what: The 'Empty table' state test only checks `/`. The state table says the empty-table message applies to any filter. The AC-7 test does check every filter.
findings.fix: Optionally loop over the filtered views in the state test.

lenses.note: The change matches the spec and PR words. It adds the migration, label, filter, nav, 400 and traffic route, and nothing outside the spec.
All 8 acceptance items are named by tests. The Decisions are followed: existing items get normal, and only high and low are labelled. The follow-up commit does not edit the spec.
One assertion was loosened to one that can never fail (see the finding). I did not run the tests; CI runs them.
The README describes the filter. Nothing stale found.
The query is parameterised, the Set check on priority is correct, and titles are escaped. The empty-table check adds one extra COUNT query only when a filter matches nothing.
Input is validated against an allow-list and bound as a parameter. The route regex still refuses spaces and #. No planted instructions found.
The page is minimal and the nav is plain HTML, with nothing beyond what the spec asks. No layout or visual change to review.
No screenshots or browser were available. The UI is a plain server-rendered list, covered by markup tests.
The 'Tests deleted or loosened: none' claim is false (see the finding). The other claims match the diff.
